prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical discovery of the Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I keep B040 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, and my reasons have not changed since round 1. The Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal define a state of matter by topology, and the HgTe quantum-well experiment was the original observation: quantized edge conductance of 2e^2/h that depended on gate voltage and device width as predicted. The theory-to-experiment chain is traceable, and it has been confirmed for about fifteen years by independent transport and spectroscopy, so I am as close to absolutely sure of the topic as this committee ever gets. The reading of the round-1 record that matters most to me is that three of us arrived at the same trio independently, and that the two colleagues who disagreed with my opening position (Eriksson and Mehlig) did so on the substance of who originated the mechanism, not on a count. That is the argument that moved me, and it is why I accepted Mele in place of Hasan. On the question of whether this is distinct from 2016: Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz were rewarded for topological phases and transitions in the integer quantum Hall setting and in 1D and 2D models, whereas this prize would recognise time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, a new class that exists without a magnetic field and that was observed in a real material. I regard that as a separate discovery and the citation should say so by naming the Z2 invariant and the HgTe observation.
statement.case_against: The credit remains imperfect and I will not pretend otherwise. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal told Molenkamp which material and which quantum-well thickness to use, and Zhang is deceased, so a decisive step falls outside the three names. Hasan's group made the first spectroscopy of a three-dimensional topological insulator, which is the point at which the field became a materials discovery, and the three-person cap leaves it out. Priority among other early ARPES groups and the Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents theory also cannot be fully checked from the supplied text. The citation must therefore be worded around the Z2 classification and the first observation of the quantum spin Hall state, not around the first prediction of HgTe or the first 3D observation. If the committee prefers a credit that is fair to both the 2D and 3D stories, B040 is the hardest ballot to make defensible in three names, and B045 has the cleaner credit. My concern is also that a prize on B045 would reward a measurement that was done better, which under the discovery criterion carries less weight for me than a phenomenon that had not been seen before.

responses.point: Mehlig would drop Hasan before Mele because his ARPES work confirms a prediction by Fu, Kane and Mele and by Moore and Balents, while accepting my trio if 3D materials carry more weight than the theory partnership.
responses.response: I accept this and have stopped pressing for Hasan in the third seat. I still think it is a closer call than you suggest, since a prediction that nobody has seen in a real crystal is not yet a discovery, and the Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 spectroscopy was the first observation of a protected surface state. But the committee has to choose, and Kane and Mele are the originators of the classification from which the 3D case follows, with Kane himself a co-author of the 3D theory. The trio therefore does cover the 3D theory through Kane, and the experimental credit goes to the first observation of the effect, which is Molenkamp. I would ask that the citation make clear that the 3D materials work is not being declared secondary, and I would record the Hasan point in the committee's notes and not hide it.

responses.point: Eriksson takes the Hasan argument seriously but regards dropping Mele as hard to defend, and would keep the theory pair plus Molenkamp, or consider Hasan replacing Molenkamp if 3D is judged essential, though that weakens the clear quantum spin Hall narrative.
responses.response: I agree with your reasoning and with the conclusion that replacing Molenkamp with Hasan would break the clearest chain on the table. The reason I would not do it is the one I use for every candidate: the HgTe measurement is the original experiment on the effect Kane and Mele predicted, and it is the more decisive of the two because it tests a quantitative prediction, the 2e^2/h edge conductance, rather than mapping a band structure. Your acknowledgement that ARPES links experiment to calculation is fair, but a spectroscopic map shows surface states exist, whereas the transport result shows they carry protected current. I also take your point on 2016 and would add that the citation should name the Z2 invariant, since that is what distinguishes this from the earlier prize.

responses.point: Pearce, the Chair and an IceCube supporter, says the attribution to Halzen and Karle is untidy because of AMANDA and other leaders, would cite only the diffuse flux, and says that if the committee wants consensus B045 is probably it.
responses.response: I respect that you named the attribution weakness in your own first choice, and I agree the citation should rest on the diffuse flux and not on TXS 0506+056 or NGC 1068. Where I differ is on your consensus argument. B045 is named most often as an alternative, but that is also what an acceptable second choice looks like, and I do not treat support counts as a substitute for judging which discovery is more original. B045 has the cleanest credit, which I acknowledge, but a better clock built on the comb and on ion control is a refinement of a measurement that earlier prizes already covered, whereas B040 and your own B016 both opened something that had not been seen. If B040 fails on attribution I would move to B045 as the committee's compromise, and I would be comfortable with that, but I do not think it is the strongest scientific case.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the optical lattice clock is distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes because it addresses Doppler and recoil limits differently, that the redefinition of the second is not required for the physics, and that Katori and Ye form a clean two-name credit.
responses.response: Your answer on distinctness is the strongest argument for B045 in the record, and it has made me more comfortable with it as my first alternative. The magic-wavelength trap is a real invention, not only a better number, and I agree that the redefinition of the second should not be a condition. What I cannot get past, from the supplied text, is the priority issue you also raise: Takamoto, Lemonde and the SYRTE group demonstrated early strontium lattice clocks, and Katori's priority for the concept needs to be checked in the record before I am absolutely sure the two names did the original work. For B040 the equivalent doubt is the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, so I do not claim my candidate is cleaner, only that the original experiment is unambiguous there and less clear here.

responses.point: Danielsson regards the diffuse flux alone as sufficient for B016 but says the prize would be premature if source identification must be independently confirmed, and treats B045 as the safer alternative.
responses.response: I agree that the diffuse flux, seen in several independent channels, is sufficient for a discovery, and I do not think the source identification needs to be settled first. That keeps B016 as my second alternative. My remaining question is the same as yours: whether Halzen and Karle are the two who did the original work. The historical record of AMANDA and of who led the first discovery analyses is exactly what I would want to see before voting for it, and from the supplied text I cannot establish it. If the committee can show that record, I would move B016 above B045 as my fallback.

uncertainties: Whether the historical record on Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 would make the committee regard Hasan's 3D spectroscopy as an original discovery that cannot be left out, even at the cost of Mele.
Whether the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, with Zhang deceased, makes the credit for the HgTe experiment unfair in a three-person configuration, and whether the citation wording can avoid that.
Whether the committee accepts B040 as distinct from the 2016 topological-phases prize once the citation names the Z2 invariant and the HgTe observation.

For the alternatives, the priority of Katori against Takamoto, Lemonde and SYRTE (B045), and the split of credit among Halzen, Karle, AMANDA and other IceCube leaders (B016), neither of which I can settle from the supplied text.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: I have no documented collaboration with Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan or any person credited on B045 or B016, and no recusal-level conflict on my preferred configuration or alternatives. My Chalmers colleague Goran Johansson, who works on superconducting circuits, has disclosed a conflict on B026 and possibly B008, which are not in my configuration. I note only that my field, electron microscopy, is a materials characterisation field adjacent to topological materials, which gives me an experimental taste but no personal tie.
